section_summary: This section traces disputes over Japanese external assets, occupation costs, currency, gold, and credits in 1947. It includes policy memoranda and telegrams, Burma’s law for valuing wartime Japanese currency, and detailed accounts for the Allied trusteeship of former Japanese Embassy funds and property in Buenos Aires.

subfiles.title: Draft letter to Mr. Atcheson
subfiles.about: Suggests revising a reply about Japanese assets in Soviet-controlled areas.
subfiles.summary: Borton questions whether Tokyo's valuation changes the allocation of Japanese external assets.

subfiles.title: Japanese assets in Siam
subfiles.about: Clarifies United States policy on vesting Japanese assets in Siam and meeting Allied claims.
subfiles.summary: Lacy assures British Embassy official Everson that Allied claims are not capped by the value of vested assets.

subfiles.title: Currency conversion memorandum sent to Dr. Bunce
subfiles.about: Forwards a currency conversion memorandum and discusses Dean Bowman's visit to Korea.
subfiles.summary: Jones sends copies for distribution and recommends a roundtable for Bowman.

subfiles.title: Approval of amendment to SWNCC 236/38
subfiles.about: Recommends approval of amendments concerning Japanese external assets.
subfiles.summary: Forwards proposed amendments and Silver's explanation.

subfiles.title: Revision of SWNCC 236/38
subfiles.about: Requests adoption of revisions to the Japanese external assets study.
subfiles.summary: Asks the committee to amend SWNCC 236/38 as enclosed.

subfiles.title: Reasons for amendment to SWNCC 236/38
subfiles.about: Explains proposed changes in the use and disposition of Japanese assets in neutral countries and Turkey.
subfiles.summary: Silver broadens interim occupation uses and withdraws a proposed concession concerning gold in Japan.

subfiles.title: Proposed amendment to SWNCC 236/38
subfiles.about: Revises conclusions on Japanese assets held in named countries.
subfiles.summary: The draft keeps proceeds abroad for SCAP-directed occupation uses, ultimately financing imports to prevent disease and unrest.

subfiles.title: Proposed amendments to Japanese public finance conclusions
subfiles.about: Proposes revisions on public enterprise audits and local tax powers.
subfiles.summary: Changes respond to SCAP comments on Japanese public finance.

subfiles.title: Disposition of assets of societies and institutions
subfiles.about: Questions how overseas creditor claims against controlled Japanese institutions will be validated.
subfiles.summary: The author supports one property proposal but seeks safeguards against wartime claims aiding Japan.

subfiles.title: French and Italian yen balances in Japan
subfiles.about: Recommends circulating the State Department's alternative paper on French and Italian yen balances.
subfiles.summary: Asks the committee to consider the attached State memorandum in place of SWNCC 366.

subfiles.title: Japanese Currency (Evaluation) Act despatch
subfiles.about: Transmits Burma's law valuing Japanese occupation currency for specified debts.
subfiles.summary: Reports graduated values ranging from parity for 1942 debts to five Burmese rupees per hundred Japanese rupees for 1945.

subfiles.title: Japanese Currency (Evaluation) Act, 1947
subfiles.about: Sets legal conversion values for Japanese occupation notes in settling wartime debts.
subfiles.summary: The act gives conversion rates by year for unpaid occupation-era debts, addresses court decrees, and recognizes accepted wartime payments at face value.

subfiles.title: Foreign investment and yen balances
subfiles.about: Raises concerns about using existing yen balances to acquire new interests in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Oliver compares Germany's moratorium and asks to discuss the proposed cable.

subfiles.title: Suggested radio on foreign investment in Japan
subfiles.about: Proposes asking SCAP whether to restrict investment made with yen balances.
subfiles.summary: A draft message cites Germany's occupation-zone moratorium as a possible model.

subfiles.title: Allied Powers Trusteeship Japanese Funds quarterly accounts
subfiles.about: Transmits April–June 1947 accounts and a receipt for trusteeship custody in Buenos Aires.
subfiles.summary: Reports sale of nearly all remaining former Japanese Embassy furniture and equipment.

subfiles.title: Trusteeship account current, April–June 1947
subfiles.about: Records trusteeship balances, sale receipts, and disbursements.
subfiles.summary: Itemizes official and alleged private Japanese funds.

subfiles.title: Sales voucher for former Japanese Embassy property
subfiles.about: Certifies three sales of former Japanese Embassy equipment.
subfiles.summary: Lists sales to Flores, auction purchasers, and the Chinese Embassy.

subfiles.title: Receipt for Underwood typewriter
subfiles.about: Acknowledges purchase and payment for a former Japanese Embassy typewriter.
subfiles.summary: Spanish and English text confirms the Underwood sale.

subfiles.title: Auction sale accounting
subfiles.about: Accounts for a May 28 auction of former Japanese Embassy furnishings.
subfiles.summary: The translated and original schedules list lots, prices, taxes, expenses, and net proceeds.

subfiles.title: Auction expense account
subfiles.about: Itemizes transport, advertising, personnel, and other auction expenses.
subfiles.summary: The translated statement and Spanish original support the auction expense total.

subfiles.title: Auction firm's terms
subfiles.about: Offers terms for selling trusteeship furniture.
subfiles.summary: Quotes a ten percent commission and separate transport arrangements.

subfiles.title: Ungaro y Barbará auction arrangements
subfiles.about: Discusses advertising and other costs for the planned auction.
subfiles.summary: Lists newspaper advertisement prices and related sale preparations.

subfiles.title: Auction notice in La Prensa
subfiles.about: Advertises an auction of office furniture and safes.
subfiles.summary: Announces the exhibition and sale of trusteeship property.

subfiles.title: Sale to Chinese Embassy
subfiles.about: Records sale of typewriters, filing cabinets, and a safe.
subfiles.summary: The receipt lists prices, explains the valuations, and notes consent from the four interested embassies.

subfiles.title: Scharer safe offer
subfiles.about: Offers 850 Argentine pesos for a safe.
subfiles.summary: The firm offers to pay removal costs.

subfiles.title: Borges safe offer
subfiles.about: Offers 950 Argentine pesos for a safe.
subfiles.summary: The firm offers cash and transport at its expense.

subfiles.title: Typewriter purchase offer
subfiles.about: Quotes purchase prices for four typewriters.
subfiles.summary: Provides a price for each machine and a total offer.

subfiles.title: Bradford typewriter offer
subfiles.about: Offers prices for four Underwood typewriters.
subfiles.summary: The firm declines to quote on the safe.

subfiles.title: Flores typewriter and safe offer
subfiles.about: Quotes purchase prices for four typewriters and a safe.
subfiles.summary: Lists bids for equipment inspected at the American and Chinese embassies.

subfiles.title: Trusteeship disbursements, April–June 1947
subfiles.about: Lists cable, moving-tip, and storage payments.
subfiles.summary: Records 261.56 Argentine pesos in official-fund disbursements.

subfiles.title: Argentine stamped receipt
subfiles.about: Contains a stamped Argentine receipt associated with the accounts.
subfiles.summary: The surviving OCR gives no reliable transaction details.

subfiles.title: Cable company invoice
subfiles.from: All America Cables and Radio Inc.
subfiles.about: Bills a cable to Washington concerning Japanese civilian repatriation.
subfiles.summary: Shows a charge of 54.56 Argentine pesos.

subfiles.title: Japanese civilian repatriation cable
subfiles.about: Reports a shipping company's reluctance to carry Japanese civilians from Buenos Aires.
subfiles.summary: Suggests the Department seek reversal of the company's decision.

subfiles.title: Receipt for movers' tips
subfiles.about: Acknowledges reimbursement for movers' tips.
subfiles.summary: Records ten Argentine pesos.

subfiles.title: La Continental storage invoice
subfiles.about: Bills storage of a safe formerly deposited by the Swiss Legation.
subfiles.summary: Covers storage from January 1946 to May 1947.

subfiles.title: Receipt for movers' tips
subfiles.about: Acknowledges reimbursement for movers' tips.
subfiles.summary: Records five Argentine pesos.

subfiles.title: Remaining trusteeship property
subfiles.about: Inventories property retained after the furniture sale.
subfiles.summary: Lists boxes, newspapers, and card cabinets holding files on Japanese citizens in Argentina.

subfiles.title: Amendment to occupation-cost policy
subfiles.about: Proposes protecting legal import-financing obligations before applying a first charge to Japanese assets.
subfiles.summary: The amendment aims to help secure private credits for approved imports.

subfiles.title: Approval routing for SWNCC 236/49
subfiles.about: Routes the occupation-cost paper and amendment for approval.
subfiles.summary: Notes departmental clearances and McGuire's separate statement on gold.

subfiles.title: Monetary gold and first-charge principle
subfiles.about: Urges reserving Japanese monetary gold for possible reparations while recognizing its use as import-loan security.
subfiles.summary: FN supports the legal first-charge principle but recommends taking gold for United States costs only as a last resort.

subfiles.title: Routing McGuire's gold memorandum
subfiles.about: Seeks a procedure for keeping FN's gold position in the SWNCC 236/49 record.
subfiles.summary: McGuire recommends wider concurrence; a handwritten response treats the comments as a departmental statement.

subfiles.title: Currency arrangements for business visitors to Japan
subfiles.about: Requests War Department concurrence in a reply to SCAP on acceptable currencies.
subfiles.summary: Explains Treasury and State contributions to the attached cable.

subfiles.title: Reply to SCAP on acceptable currencies
subfiles.about: Defines currencies acceptable for visiting businesspeople's expenses and yen purchases.
subfiles.summary: The draft reviews convertibility and exchange controls country by country. It advises using similar acceptance criteria for currencies tendered to buy yen and Japanese exports.

subfiles.title: Reference slip for currency cable
subfiles.about: Transmits attachments following a telephone conversation.
subfiles.summary: Refers to the currency cable file.

subfiles.title: Handwritten note on cable wording
subfiles.about: Comments on wording in the proposed SCAP currency reply.
subfiles.summary: The OCR is too damaged to establish the requested change securely.

subfiles.title: Assignment of reply to SCAP C-54505
subfiles.about: Forwards Treasury's proposed telegram responding to SCAP's currency inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Identifies the attached draft as the proposed reply.

subfiles.title: Earlier draft cable to SCAP
subfiles.about: Reviews convertible currencies and proposed rules for business visitors buying yen.
subfiles.summary: The draft lists IMF members and exchange-control conditions, then adds State and War comments seeking consistent criteria for yen and export payments.

subfiles.title: SCAP reply on inconvertible currencies
subfiles.about: Explains planned acceptance of usable inconvertible currencies in Japanese trade.
subfiles.summary: SCAP will amend its instructions but seeks to avoid large inconvertible balances; British representatives cannot confirm sterling convertibility.

subfiles.title: SCAP plan for business visitors' currency
subfiles.about: Sets proposed rules for payment certificates, yen conversion, lodging, services, and business facilities.
subfiles.summary: SCAP proposes that visitors buy military payment certificates with dollars or acceptable currencies and obtain yen at a temporary military conversion rate. It requests advice on freely convertible currencies and details charges and facilities available to traders.

subfiles.title: Gold and silver revolving fund; FEC committee progress
subfiles.about: Records British views on pledging Japanese gold and silver and on progress of an FEC paper.
subfiles.summary: Everson accepts SCAP's use of the fund as collateral if done in good faith, while cautioning against moving gold abroad. He and Whitman also discuss speeding FEC committee action and petroleum-refining limits.

subfiles.title: Request to present occupation-cost policy to FEC
subfiles.about: Requests authority to present SWNCC 236/49 to the Far Eastern Commission promptly.
subfiles.summary: McCoy says presentation would address Allied concerns and help negotiations over revolving-fund collateral.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of occupation-cost policy to Treasury
subfiles.about: Forwards the approved United States policy on Japanese occupation costs.
subfiles.summary: Transmits SANACC 236/51 for information.

subfiles.title: SANACC 236/51 transmittal
subfiles.about: Sends approved occupation-cost policy copies for distribution.
subfiles.summary: Requests forwarding copies to Justice, Treasury, and the United States FEC member.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of occupation-cost policy to Attorney General
subfiles.about: Forwards approved United States policy on Japanese occupation costs.
subfiles.summary: Transmits SANACC 236/51 for information.

subfiles.title: Instruction to introduce occupation-cost policy at FEC
subfiles.to: United States member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Directs submission of SANACC 236/51 to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Reports Army concurrence in introducing the policy at the earliest practicable date.

subfiles.title: Army concurrence on FEC submission
subfiles.about: Confirms Army has no objection to presenting the occupation-cost policy to FEC nations.
subfiles.summary: Approves introduction at the earliest practicable time.

subfiles.title: Instruction to General McCoy on external assets
subfiles.about: Requests presentation of an attached policy statement to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Directs McCoy to seek adoption while making no mention of Turkey for the time being.

subfiles.title: Japanese assets in Afghanistan
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Kabul
subfiles.about: Provides requested values and exchange rates for assets in Afghanistan.
subfiles.summary: Lists amounts in Afghanis and several foreign currencies with dollar conversions.

subfiles.title: Handwritten calculation note
subfiles.about: Requests checking dollar conversions in the preceding Afghanistan letter.
subfiles.summary: The OCR preserves only fragments of the note.

subfiles.title: Japanese Currency (Evaluation) Act follow-up
subfiles.about: Forwards copies of Burma's Japanese Currency (Evaluation) Act.
subfiles.summary: States that the act governs settlement of debts contracted during Japanese occupation.

subfiles.title: Withdrawal of SANACC 366
subfiles.about: Requests withdrawal of the paper on French and Italian yen balances in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Asks that SANACC 366 leave committee consideration.

subfiles.title: Disposition of French and Italian yen balances
subfiles.about: Explains why the Italian yen-balance issue no longer appears to require action.
subfiles.summary: Concurs in referring remaining issues to the Far Eastern Commission and withdrawing the older paper.

subfiles.title: Japanese assets in Afghanistan despatch routing
subfiles.about: Forwards the Kabul despatch on Japanese assets in Afghanistan.
subfiles.summary: Sends despatch 259 to JK for appropriate action.
